entry.evidence: but there are few researches to investigate the geothermal potentiality

steps.action: The authors pose the aim: map the subsurface structure of the Abu Gharadig Basin and its relevance to geothermal resources, using airborne potential-field data and well temperatures.
steps.quote: The purpose of current research is to examine the subsurface structure of AGB and its relevance to the presence of geothermal energy resources

steps.action: They take the basin's structural and stratigraphic framework and the premise that faults and structures control geothermal fluids from published geology.
steps.quote: geothermal fields are dependent on faults and structures because fluids often move via fissures in the underground rocks

steps.action: They assemble GETECH airborne Bouguer gravity and total magnetic intensity grids and bottom-hole temperature records from 138 oil and gas wells.
steps.quote: The current study also include temperature well records from 138 wells that ranging in depth from 2000 to 4800 m

steps.action: They correct the BHT readings with the Waples et al. (2004) formula and compute well-based temperature gradients (0.022-0.034 °C/m) and heat flow (43-84 mW/m2) with literature conductivities.
steps.quote: An empirical formula develop by Waples et al. (54) was applied to our data in order to make the corrections.

steps.action: They reduce the magnetic grid to the pole and compute radially averaged power spectra in 48 overlapping windows. They estimate top and centroid depths and derive Curie point depths of 17-21 km (Zb = 2Z0 - Zt).
steps.quote: the area was divided into 48 overlapping square sub-areas (windows) with diameters of (87 × 113 km)

steps.action: From the CPDs, assuming 580 °C at the Curie depth, k = 2.0 W/mK and no radioactive heat sources, they derive gradient and heat flow maps (0.026-0.034 °C/m; 52-67 mW/m2).
steps.quote: The values of geothermal gradients are between 0.026 and 0.034 °C/m and an average of nearby 0.03 °C/m.

steps.action: They invert the Bouguer gravity with GRABLOX as a two-layer height inversion (densities 2.2 and 2.67 g/cm3, Occam regularization, second-order polynomial base anomaly) to map basement depth (4.5-7 km). They report the misfit (RMS 0.007).
steps.quote: The conducted model has a Root Mean Square (RMS) value of 0.007.

steps.action: They compare the inverted sediment thickness with well data along a profile through well GPAA-3, a well that does not reach the basement.
steps.quote: A high correlation exists between the depth of the expected basement depending on a 3D gravity inversion and well data.

steps.action: They compare the basin's CPDs with Tanaka et al.'s (1999) ranges by tectonic setting and find stable-continent geothermal conditions despite the basin's unstable-shelf setting.
steps.quote: It does, however, have geothermal conditions comparable to those seen on stable continents.

steps.action: They regress BHT-measured gradients on CPD-derived gradients (44 points, R2 = 0.90) to validate the magnetic estimates.
steps.quote: [...] from CPDs and those from BHT are highly correlated, with roughly 90% agreement (Fig. 13).

steps.action: They plot CPD and basement depth along an E-W profile and note that shallow Curie depths coincide with basement uplifts and high heat flow.
steps.quote: Shallow CPD and uplifts in the Precambrian basement rocks were found to have a link

steps.action: They keep the CPD, gradient, heat-flow and basement maps and the interpretation that basement rocks control the basin's geothermal potential.
steps.quote: Combining the findings shows a consistency between shallow curie depths, uplifts on basement rocks, and locations of higher heat flow

No; CPD, crustal gradients and basement depth are latent, inferred from potential fields
Map CPD, gradients, heat flow and basement depth for geothermal assessment
Conditions found: compiled airborne grids and BHT logs from existing oil wells
Checked against BHT gradients (R2 0.90) and one well section; no sensitivity tests

end.claim: Spectral analysis of aeromagnetic data, 3D gravity inversion and corrected BHT data give, for the Abu Gharadig Basin, Curie depths of about 17-21 km, gradients of 0.022-0.034 °C/m, heat flow of 43-84 mW/m2 and basement depths of 4.5-7 km, with shallow Curie depths co-located with basement uplifts and high heat flow.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the windowed power-spectrum estimation of Curie point depths from the aeromagnetic grid, there would be no crustal thermal maps to validate or to correlate with basement relief.

gates.evidence: The data were compiled from existing GETECH grids and oil-well BHT logs, not acquired to test a hypothesis (§3 ¶1-2). The CPD-derived gradients could have disagreed with the BHT gradients (§6 ¶2), and basement depth was compared with one well that does not reach basement (§5 ¶4). The basement-control interpretation faced no test it could fail. Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: Curie temperature: the ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition used to define the Curie point depth
radially averaged power spectrum analysis of gridded data
Occam's principle: minimizing model roughness and data misfit together

limits: No review file or earlier version was supplied, so only a final-paper sequence is coded. Composition none_fits: this is a regional estimation survey. Conditions are found, no rivals are stated, no regularity with a range is fitted, and no new capability is built, so neither trace_series nor natures_repetition applies. Headline status is estimate_with_resolution, but no uncertainties are given. Resolution appears only through the window size and the L/4π depth limit (§4.2 ¶2), so even this status is generous. Sub-claims and their statuses: (a) basement rocks are primarily responsible for the geothermal potential (§7 ¶2). This is at most best_explanation, with no rivals stated and support resting only on visual co-location along one profile (Fig. 14). (b) The sedimentary cover may be free of radioactive heat sources (§6 ¶4). Status none, and partly circular, since the heat-flow calculation already assumed no radioactive source (§4.2 ¶4). (c) Low-temperature hydrothermal resources exist (§6 ¶2). Status none; inferred from average values only. Internal inconsistencies, inferred from comparing sections: the abstract ranges (CPD 17-22 km, gradients 25-34 °C/km, heat flow 52-86 mW/m2) differ from the results (CPD 17-21 km, gradients 0.022-0.034 °C/m, heat flow 43-84 and 52-67 mW/m2). The conclusions call CPDs of '> 19 km' the shallower ones. The 90% agreement is an R2 on 44 points, although 138 wells are listed. Average BHT heat flow (72 mW/m2) differs from CPD heat flow (60 mW/m2), and the paper does not discuss this. BHT heat flow used conductivities of 1.8-2.6 W/m°C, while CPD heat flow used 2.0. Prior CPD maps of the same region (Saada 2016; Elbarbary et al. 2018) are cited, but the new estimates are not compared with them (inference). No sensitivity tests were run for window size, Curie temperature, conductivity or density contrast. The Demerdash et al. (1984) reference cited for basin geology is an electrical-machines paper, apparently a citation error. Data are available only on request.

disagreements.target: Expectation from the basin's position on the unstable shelf zone (Schlumberger, 1984) under the CPD-by-setting ranges of Tanaka et al. (1999)
disagreements.support: The basin's CPDs of 17-19 km fall in Tanaka et al.'s stable-continent range despite its tectonically active unstable-shelf setting.
disagreements.quote: It does, however, have geothermal conditions comparable to those seen on stable continents.
